summary: On SolidCraft's earlier kernel, fillets and chamfers too large for the faces beside their edge (running into a pocket, or two blends crossing on a narrow face) were built through instead of refused (#1080). The fix refuses them with the largest size that fits; these cases keep the sizes that do fit building, with closed-form volumes: chamfers 2 and 4 and a round 3 on the edge beside a pocket 4 mm in, both top edges of a 4 mm rib at 1.5 (they would meet at 2), and the four top edges of a cube at 5, which mitre at the corners and must not be refused for overlapping there. Two more cases take the test's too-large sizes into the pocket (chamfer 6, round 5) with the cliff overflow (`fillet_refuse_rails_leaving_faces`, `fillet_cliff_overflow`, tangency-labs/solidcore#960): built as if the faces went on, removing exactly what lies in the body. The runner cannot require a refusal, so the rib's crossing chamfer and round of 3 are not ported, nor its SolidCraft-only volume guard; its #1668 and concentric-round tests are already 1668-round-both-sides-of-wall.json and tangency-labs/solidcore#683.

cases.name: chamfer_beside_pocket_2
cases.note: Chamfer 2 on the top edge at x = 40 of a 40 x 20 x 20 block with a 10 x 10 pocket 10 deep, 4 mm in from that edge. Up to the pocket's rim it fits: the triangle along the 20 mm edge.

cases.name: chamfer_beside_pocket_4
cases.note: Chamfer 4 on the top edge at x = 40 of a 40 x 20 x 20 block with a 10 x 10 pocket 10 deep, 4 mm in from that edge. Up to the pocket's rim it fits: the triangle along the 20 mm edge. The chamfer's rail on the top face then runs along the pocket's rim, so it opts in to `fillet_rail_rim_on_face` (WR-301, tangency-labs/solidcore#485); the pinned SMLib fails it with 1001 ("Unable to Process Rollover").

cases.name: fillet_beside_pocket_3
cases.note: Round r 3 on the same edge: it fits short of the pocket (the largest that fits is 4).

cases.name: rib_chamfers_1_5
cases.note: Both top edges of a 40 x 4 x 20 rib chamfered 1.5, below the 2 at which they would meet in the middle of the top face.

cases.name: rib_fillets_1_5
cases.note: Both top edges of the rib rounded r 1.5.

cases.name: cube_top_chamfers_meet_at_corners
cases.note: The four top edges of a 20 mm cube chamfered 5: they mitre at the corners and are not refused for overlapping there. The top 5 mm is a frustum from 20 x 20 to 10 x 10.

cases.name: cube_top_fillets_meet_at_corners
cases.note: The four top edges of the cube rounded r 5, the vertical edges sharp: the rounds mitre at the corners, so each horizontal section of the top 5 mm is a square inset by 5 - sqrt(25 - t^2) at t below the round's top.

cases.name: chamfer_6_runs_into_the_pocket
cases.note: Chamfer 6 on the same edge, past the pocket's rim: SolidCraft refuses it as too large (the largest that fits is 4). With the cliff overflow it is built as if the faces went on and only what lies in the body is removed: the 6 mm triangle along the 20 mm edge less its part over the pocket. Without the flags the pinned SMLib returns success with nothing removed and a body that is not a manifold solid.

removed.formula: 0.5*6^2*20 - 2*10 (the triangle's part over the pocket: x 34..36, z >= 54 - x, y 5..15)

cases.name: fillet_5_runs_into_the_pocket
cases.note: Round 5 on the same edge, past the pocket's rim: SolidCraft refuses it (the largest that fits is 4). With the cliff overflow the round is built as if the faces went on and only what lies in the body is removed. Without the flags the pinned SMLib returns success with nothing removed and a non-manifold body.

removed.formula: (1 - pi/4)*5^2*20 - 10*(5 - (sqrt(24)/2 + 12.5*asin(1/5))) (the round's corner less its part over the pocket, x 35..36, y 5..15)
